$comment: 01.7.1-T4.2 (AC6): vulnerability-scan allowlist consumed by scripts/audit-deps.sh and scripts/audit_deps_eval.py. Keyed by advisory id (GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz or CVE-YYYY-NNNNN — the last path segment of the advisory URL from 'npm audit --json' or 'dotnet list package --vulnerable --format json'). Every entry must name the accepting ADR (adr), the affected package, and the reason; 'expires' (YYYY-MM-DD) is optional for an unscoped entry but REQUIRED once 'scope' is present — an expired or undated scoped exception never exempts. 'scope' is optional and npm-only: {"npm": [{"workspace": "<workspace name>", "via": "<direct dependency>"}]} narrows the exemption to those (origin, direct dependency) pairs over the package-lock.json graph: every production chain from the root package or a declared workspace to the finding's real package must start with a listed pair, and the 'via' record must be the registry package of that name (no alias, file:, git or link). Anything the lock cannot prove — unreadable lock, unresolvable required edge, an npm audit node the lock does not record as that package — is a scanner failure (exit 2), never an exemption. The scope constrains those two hops only; it does not show how the package is invoked, and the exception files are PR-editable, so review of this file, the gate scripts and the lock is the real control. An unscoped entry behaves as before: advisory id plus a live ADR is enough.
